result.report:
PASS for the exact stated partial scope, subject to the harmless textual corrections below. The generator-contact certificate, its finite PCC-witness variant, the triangle-square family, and the restricted obstacle/reference extensions are established. This does not establish the arbitrary-data product theorem, the original classification, or a negative-integral counterexample.

I checked the cited definitions and relevant proof boundaries against the authentic [BMPS v1 PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.08664v1). The essential mathematics is reconstructed in the supplied argument; the source theorems, predecessor cylinder argument, book comparisons, receipts, and execution claims are not theorem premises. The real scalar extension is explicit: on a fixed finite rational structure, continuity imposes rational linear equations, so real PA functions are spanned by literal PA functions after clearing slope denominators. This does not permit irrational spatial walls.

The generator comparison is genuinely global. The homogenization argument establishes the finite vertex/recession-generator decomposition for every nonempty pointed rational cell. For a raw competitor q, bounded reference difference gives a uniform bound q≤H+M. Replacing a small portion of a positive vertex coefficient by rational endpoints v*+Rr_j preserves the barycentre exactly, even at irrational centres. The resulting same-cell PCC gives q(x)≤H(x)+MΣμ_j/R, hence q≤H without assuming continuity. Actual PC and the growth/obstacle bounds make H a global competitor. Tight witness PCCs supply exactly the missing vertex bounds; the acyclic propagation variant follows by induction.

The divisor algebra checks out, including saturated quotient lattices, independence of normal lifts, locality, refinement, balancing, and commutativity. The representatives s/χ are used modulo tangential directions; they need not themselves be integral lifts. The symmetric second-divisor formula follows directly from (5). The product expansion retains the factor 2 in dimension two and the stated d! normalization. The PC-to-PAPC proof covers every positive dimension and every ordinary open: the nonnegative incident balancing cone has a rational generating section, and rational balanced vectors produce genuine small-endpoint PCCs. Linearity then covers all real cycle weights.

For the graph, the outgoing directions balance with unit weights, have rank two, and generate the saturated vertex lattices; their relation kernels are precisely the positive unit-weight rays. The bounded cycle remains present. The product has dimension two, unit product weights, and saturated direct-product cell lattices. Ambient convexity proves every actual PCC inequality for γ and H, including remote endpoints and real centres. All nonzero recession directions have positive reference slope. The bounds 0≤H−γ≤cr and 0≤u≤(c+η)r+ε/2 establish the required bounded differences.

The rational level r cuts exactly the nine products of A-incident edges. Their complex has the stated fifteen vertices. The tent adds only (M,M). Thus arbitrary real c, η, and ε introduce no irrational walls. The junction witness has barycentre (A,A): its weights (1/4,1/4,1/2) cancel the three first-factor displacements exactly, and its endpoints are contact points with H=cr. This establishes the raw envelope despite noncontact at that junction.

The recursive measure calculation is complete. Globally, the first cycle has weight c gcd(a_i,b_j) on each of the nine cut segments. Coordinate junction fibres have weight cκ_V wherever H=γ and zero on their portions inside the flat region. Other first-face coefficients vanish. At original pairs other than (A,A), the second coefficient is 2c²κ_Vκ_W, with κ=(4,2,2). At each cut junction, the actual plane indices are b/d_i, a_i/d_i, and 1; index-two cones occur. The first coefficients are cd_i on R_i and 4c on z, with zero on −z and h_i, and their balancing vector vanishes. The second coefficient is consequently 4c²b.

Therefore the positive atoms are four of mass 16c², four of mass 8c², four of mass 4c², and two of mass 8c², totaling 128c². The coefficients at (A,A) and (M,M) are zero. Along cut-segment interiors H is constant on the first cycle; elsewhere the local affine structure and refinement cancellation exclude additional atoms. This accounts for rectangle interiors, edge and junction fibres, artificial vertices, and all ends. Contact at the fourteen atoms makes the complete integral zero. The decreasing sequence H+1/j converges uniformly, remains PAPC in the same growth class, and has identical recursive measures.

The mixed differences cr for H and ε/2 for u establish nonseparability. The rectangle-centre PCC violates Jensen for f, so f is not PC. For every prescribed bounded nonnegative real-PA lift vanishing at the fourteen atoms, the same witness and generator comparison remain valid; additional domain vertices carry no mass. A bounded reference change preserves the competitor set and growth class when the changed reference satisfies the stated PC and positive-growth hypotheses.

Harmless corrections: in the balancing explanation, the cancelling contribution is (ω/χ)(a(s)r−a(r)s), not the printed expression with a plus sign; this follows immediately from (5). Also, cutting a corner from a bounded product square leaves a pentagonal remainder, so “trapezoids” should be corrected. Neither correction changes a hypothesis, coefficient, or proof strategy.
